attrs.definition: Memoize stage outputs keyed by input digest.
A failed child is re-dispatched up to a bounded retry budget.
Each participant produces a first artifact without seeing any other participant's draft. Shared context is withheld until the submission barrier.
The parent blocks until every dispatched child reports a terminal state. Missing a handle is a defect, not a skip.
The same event log plus the same inputs must reproduce the same plan byte-for-byte. Sampling is forbidden.
Exactly one writer owns the output path. A second writer is a collision, not a merge.
The live harness session is a mutex. A second controller must not mutate the same control plane.
A child is launched without a join handle. The parent does not wait and must not read a result that was never collected.
A named gate waits for an owner decision before proceeding.
Token draws use a non-zero temperature or an unseeded RNG; two replays of the same prompt are not required to match.
Dispatch N independent children concurrently.
A serialised checkpoint can halt and later continue the same run.
Stages run one after another; stage k+1 sees stage k outputs.
Every participant reads the live shared transcript and may condition on others' in-flight tokens.
Two workflows may issue commands into one session; the control plane is a bus, not a mutex.
Multiple writers append or overlay the same path under a shared lock or last-writer-wins rule.
The stage terminates when the first child reports SUCCESS; remaining children are cancelled.
The stage terminates only when every child has reported the same terminal class. A single dissent keeps the barrier closed.

A human gate that never sees the child's result is operationally deaf. SAT if the fire-and-forget path is a side log; not a slot clash.

attrs.definition: Memoize stage outputs keyed by input digest.
A failed child is re-dispatched up to a bounded retry budget.
Each participant produces a first artifact without seeing any other participant's draft. Shared context is withheld until the submission barrier.
The parent blocks until every dispatched child reports a terminal state. Missing a handle is a defect, not a skip.
The same event log plus the same inputs must reproduce the same plan byte-for-byte. Sampling is forbidden.
Exactly one writer owns the output path. A second writer is a collision, not a merge.
The live harness session is a mutex. A second controller must not mutate the same control plane.
A child is launched without a join handle. The parent does not wait and must not read a result that was never collected.
A named gate waits for an owner decision before proceeding.
Token draws use a non-zero temperature or an unseeded RNG; two replays of the same prompt are not required to match.
Dispatch N independent children concurrently.
A serialised checkpoint can halt and later continue the same run.
Stages run one after another; stage k+1 sees stage k outputs.
Every participant reads the live shared transcript and may condition on others' in-flight tokens.
Two workflows may issue commands into one session; the control plane is a bus, not a mutex.
Multiple writers append or overlay the same path under a shared lock or last-writer-wins rule.
The stage terminates when the first child reports SUCCESS; remaining children are cancelled.
The stage terminates only when every child has reported the same terminal class. A single dissent keeps the barrier closed.

question: Which pairs of canonical mechanisms are mutually exclusive — blind independent first pass versus shared-context deliberation, deterministic replay versus non-deterministic sampling, fire-and-forget dispatch versus a blocking fan-in barrier — and what happens today if a fusion combines them?

soft_pairs.reason: Cache keys that omit entropy will serve a stale sample as if it were a hit. The pair is SAT if the cache key includes the seed or a 'do-not-cache-stochastic' flag; it is awkward, not a slot clash.
A sequential spine can contain a parallel fan-out stage. Nesting is SAT; treating them as globally exclusive is a false HARD.
A paused parent cannot collect a fire-and-forget child that has no handle. SAT if fire-and-forget children are outside the checkpoint boundary; awkward if they are inside it.
Retries inside a human gate are SAT (retry then ask). Retries that skip the gate are a policy smell, not a slot contradiction.
A human gate that never sees the child's result is operationally deaf. SAT if the fire-and-forget path is a side log; not a slot clash.
Replay wants the cache to be a function of the log; a cache that keys only on the prompt can hide log divergence. Awkward, SAT.
A paused barrier must serialise in-flight children. SAT with a join-set in the checkpoint; awkward without one.
N parallel children plus one human gate is SAT (barrier then gate). Awkward only if the gate is duplicated per child without a fan-in.
